summary: Today’s pulse tracks California governor commutes death sentences for all 548 people on death row, Who could be behind hoax bomb threats to European air travel, and Who is Nithya Raman, the democratic socialist who will be Los Angeles’s next mayor. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are democratic, angeles, and karen. In the background, US elections 2026 live: Democrats hold nearly 100 House seats more than Republicans as blue wave continues to grow and Democratic socialist Nithya Raman wins Los Angeles mayoral race over incumbent Karen Bass keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Who is Nithya Raman, the democratic socialist who will be Los Angeles’s next mayor?
headlines.description: Urban planner and outsider who bested Karen Bass has close ties to Hollywood progressives – and a complicated relationship with the DSA Nithya Raman on Thursday unseated Los Angeles mayor Karen Bass after a neck-and-neck race for the leadership for the US’s second largest city. The young progressive’s victory means that the two largest cities in the US, as well the nation’s capital, Washington DC, have now all elected democratic socialist mayors.

headlines.description: Democrats widen gap in House chamber by flipping more seats; Ted Cruz call the US midterms election a ‘Watergate-level repudiation’ Live results | How do you feel about the results? We have put together this video capturing the key moments and offering a quick overview of one of the most important nights in US politics: The Senate race in Mississippi has become one of the most closely watched contests in the midterms, with Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democratic challenger Scott Colom separated by a remarkably narrow margin.

headlines.title: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman wins Los Angeles mayoral race over incumbent Karen Bass
headlines.description: Major shake-up as LA councilmember, once considered long shot, ousts Democratic rival she had once endorsed Nithya Raman was elected to serve as the mayor of Los Angeles, eking out a narrow win over incumbent Karen Bass, in a major shake-up in local politics that reflects the growing dissatisfaction with the direction of the city. The progressive urban planner had served on LA’s city council since 2020. She caused a stir when she entered the race earlier this year hours before the filing deadline – and shortly after endorsing Bass for re-election – and her campaign was once viewed as a long shot.

headlinePool.title: Heavy rains bring flash flooding to Georgia-Tennessee border area
headlinePool.description: Georgia governor declares local emergencies as National Weather Service issues warning: ‘Seek higher ground now!’ Severe storms brought heavy rain and flash flooding to communities across the Georgia - Tennessee border area late on Wednesday and into Thursday morning that forced dozens of rescues, despite the hazardous conditions making evacuations and efforts to save people difficult. McCaysville, in north central Georgia, was deluged with up to five inches (13cm) of rain by Thursday morning, triggering life-threatening flash flooding, the National Weather Service (NWS) said. The town lies just across the Toccoa River from Copperhill, Tennessee.

headlinePool.title: Gavin Newsom commutes more than 500 death sentences in California
headlinePool.description: Democrat’s move prevents these people from executions under future governors, after Christa Pike’s failed execution Gavin Newsom , California ’s governor, has commuted the death sentences of more than 500 people on the state’s death row on Thursday, a move that ensures they can never be executed under future administrations. The Democrat ’s mass commutation at the end of his term has converted all of the state’s death sentences to life without the possibility of parole, the largest clearing of any US death row in modern history.

headlinePool.title: ‘Our work’s not done’: Russell Brand detective urges other potential victims to come forward
headlinePool.description: Brand is under investigation over two more rape allegations and police say others could speak up after guilty verdicts The lead detective in the case against Russell Brand has urged other potential victims of the comedian to come forward after it emerged he is under investigation for two further rape allegations and faces a civil claim in the UK. Det Supt Andy Furphy, the Metropolitan police’s strategic lead in the investigation, described Brand, 51, as “a predator” whose behaviour escalated as his fame grew.

headlinePool.title: Cancer diagnoses in England hit record high of more than 1,000 people a day
headlinePool.description: While NHS is identifying more cases, it is failing to meet timescale targets on diagnosis and treatment, experts say Cancer diagnoses in England have hit record highs, with more than 1,000 people a day diagnosed, NHS figures show. But experts warned that although the health service was identifying more cases, it was still failing to meet timescale targets on diagnosis and treatment.

headlinePool.title: Paraguay’s president quits after millions of people’s savings frozen in bank crisis
headlinePool.description: Santiago Peña’s rightwing administration had authorised Ueno Bank to drastically expand operations before collapse Paraguay’s rightwing president, Santiago Peña, resigned on Thursday after a political and financial crisis collapsed the South American country’s banking system in recent days. At the centre of the crisis is Ueno Bank, which in just a few years under Peña went from an obscure digital bank to one of the country’s largest lenders, claiming to have about 60% of Paraguay’s adult population as customers.

headlinePool.title: Paraguay's president is impeached minutes after resigning following a bank collapse
headlinePool.description: Paraguayan lawmakers voted to impeach President Santiago Peña minutes after his resignation, as the collapse of a digital bank tied to his government froze millions of people's savings.

headlinePool.title: Bomb threats disrupt at least 25 flights across Europe, raising hybrid war fears
headlinePool.description: Planes forced into emergency landings or diversions two days after hoax alerts affected air travel Hoax bomb threats have caused at least 25 flights across Europe to be disrupted, with some forced to make emergency landings, as questions mount over an apparently coordinated effort to cause chaos for travellers. The series of warnings on Thursday affected flights between Italy, Ireland, the UK, Spain, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, Finland, Austria, Denmark, Belgium, Portugal, France, Greece, Serbia and Czechia.
